title: Elon Musk claims ‘I’m not Maga’ and says he regrets vast sums to back Republicans
excerpt:
Musk, who aligned with Trump and was frequent White House guest, says he feels ‘pretty foolish’ about record midterm spending

Elon Musk denied being Maga on Wednesday, despite aligning himself intens...
body_text:
Musk, who aligned with Trump and was frequent White House guest, says he feels ‘pretty foolish’ about record midterm spending

Elon Musk denied being Maga on Wednesday, despite aligning himself intensely with Donald Trump’s Make America Great Again movement since 2024.

“I’m not Maga,” the world’s richest person told the New York Times Dealbook summit, which he attended via video call from China, where he is one of several US business leaders who have accompanied Trump on his trip to Asia.

“I’m not sure what Maga means, but if that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican party, then I certainly don’t have that,” the chief executive of SpaceX and Tesla added.

Musk famously declared at a 2024 campaign rally in Madison Square Garden: “I’m not just Maga. I’m dark, gothic Maga.”

In a 45-minute interview with Andrew Ross Sorkin, a New York Times columnist, Musk also said it would be good for Washington to have split control between the two parties, and that he thinks “there are positives and negatives in both”.

He also accused Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, of “lying” about restrictions on access to his firm’s Starshield satellite system; praised Jensen Huang, the ousted Nvidia chief executive; and said that “no one I met at Anthropic set off my evil detector”.

Asked about his previous negative comments about Anthropic, Musk said that before he agreed to rent computing power to the AI firm: “I went to met with a lot of people at Anthropic. I didn’t just move forward with the deal.”

“My interaction so far with the Anthropic team is that they seem like good people and they seem principled,” Musk added. “They seem diligent and they seem seem to care about the future.”

Musk donated at least $250m of his own money to help Trump win the election in 2024, and recently spent nearly $500m in the US midterms to support Republicans, many of whom lost.

Musk admitted at the Dealbook summit that his spending had “failed”, and that he felt “pretty foolish” for spending such a sum, the most that anyone has ever spent in a political cycle when they themselves did not run for office. “It certainly shows that American elections are not just about money,” he said. “If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money.”

After Trump took office for the second time in 2025, Musk served for 180 days heading the so-called “department of government efficiency” (Doge) within Trump’s administration, before stepping down following a very public falling out with the president.

That culminated in Musk posting on his social media platform in June of that year: “Time to drop the really big bomb: @realDonaldTrump is in the Epstein files. That is the real reason they have not been made public.”

The two men later reconciled. During his time leading Doge, Musk frequently appeared in the Oval Office and at cabinet meetings alongside the president, often sporting hats that read “Make America Great Again” or “Trump was right about everything”.

title: Crimean Bridge attacked again, Russian official says
excerpt:
Final moments before stretch of Crimean Bridge collapsed after Ukrainian attack

The Crimean Bridge has been attacked by Ukraine for the third time this week, a Russian official has said.

The Moscow-...
body_text:
Final moments before stretch of Crimean Bridge collapsed after Ukrainian attack

The Crimean Bridge has been attacked by Ukraine for the third time this week, a Russian official has said.

The Moscow-installed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, confirmed that traffic was temporarily suspended following another strike on the bridge connecting mainland Russia to occupied Crimea.

The critical bridge had already been hit twice earlier in the week resulting in severe damage and part of the bridge collapsing into the water.

The important infrastructure has long been targeted by Ukraine because of its significance as a logistical and symbolic asset to Moscow's war effort.

A screengrab of the damaged Crimean bridge in the Kerch Strait on 17 November

It comes as Russian President Vladimir Putin meets US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping on Thursday for landmark talks in China.

Aksyonov confirmed the strike on the bridge in the early hours of Thursday via Telegram, adding that assessment of the damage was under way.

Meanwhile, Ukrainian sources have continued to issue air raid alert warnings overnight for districts just outside of the capital Kyiv.

At least three people were killed in a Russian drone attack on Odesa on Wednesday, according to the regional state administration. Officials described the attack as "brutal and deliberate... directly targeting people and their lives".

President Volodymyr Zelensky has called the initial strikes on the Crimean Bridge as an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making.

Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine

Ukraine used drones and missiles against it on 17 November which brought down a key section of the road.

That section of the double-arched, 12-mile bridge now lies on the seabed, brought down by an arsenal of Ukrainian long-range weaponry in a seven-stage operation culminating in a dramatic collapse.

In response, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has said the bridge "will be rebuilt, and it will be even better than before".

While Ukrainian forces have struggled to close the bridge for good, recent attempts have brought them closer to destroying the bridge's crucial road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line.

Russian forces have also targeted key bridge crossings over the Dnipro River in Kyiv in recent days.

Russian strikes hit the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges causing traffic closures, partial damage to the metro system and some power and water outages.

How the attack on Putin's prized Crimean Bridge unfolded

title: Record-breaking rain lashes California’s Bay area as ‘atmospheric river’ arrives
excerpt:
Storm expected to move into southern California, with LA residents warned of potential evacuation orders

Heavy rain pounded California’s Bay area, with record rainfall in downtown San Francisco and f...
body_text:
Storm expected to move into southern California, with LA residents warned of potential evacuation orders

Heavy rain pounded California’s Bay area, with record rainfall in downtown San Francisco and flooding and power outages across the region, as an “atmospheric river” arrived on Wednesday and dumped precipitation across the state.

The storm was expected to move into southern California on Wednesday night and Thursday, with Los Angeles warning residents in mudslide-prone areas of potential evacuation orders to come. Southern Californians were also warned of potential coastal flooding, heavy surf, wave damage to coastal piers and parking lots and beach sand erosion. Heavy snow warnings were issued for higher elevations of the Sierra Mountains, including in the Greater Lake Tahoe area.

Downtown San Francisco saw the most rainfall before noon in 76 years, at 2.11in, surpassing a record from 1950, the San Francisco Chronicle reported. By 3pm, Wednesday’s daily total of 2.28in had broken the record for the most rainfall on 18 November, which was previously set in 1918, the National Weather Service reported. South of San Francisco, in Santa Clara, there was flooding and standing water on several highways.

In San Jose, the local fire department posted on social media that two vehicles with passengers inside had become stranded in the flooded streets downtown near the SAP Center, the city’s major events arena. The second passenger was being extricated via a boat rescue, the department wrote.

Daniel Lurie, the San Francisco mayor, warned city residents the region’s winter storm and flood season, supercharged by this year’s very strong El Niño weather, was just getting started.

Despite the Wednesday afternoon break in the rain, he posted on social media, “The storm should pick back up tonight, and more rain is in the forecast for next week.”

“When these heavy storms come, we expect flooding to return to many of the same areas that were impacted this morning,” he added.

“Today’s storm certainly gave the Bay Area a good assessment of our pain points for future storms this season,” Drew Tuma, a local meteorologist for ABC7 News, wrote on social media.

Street flooding in San Francisco left maintenance hole covers floating in one neighborhood of San Francisco, while the self-driving car company Waymo temporarily suspended service in the city, the Chronicle reported. One Waymo stalled in a flooded street and blocked traffic, ABC7 News reported.

An overwhelmed sewer stormwater system also appeared to result in several “sewage geysers”, one reportedly 15-ft tall, the Chronicle reported, sharing bystander footage of the spew in the city’s Ocean Beach neighborhood.

Thousands across the Bay area were dealing with storm-related power outages by Wednesday afternoon, according to a customer outage map from Pacific Gas & Electric, the major utility company for much of northern California.

In Monterey, south of San Francisco, the local aquarium posted on social media that “storms and massive waves are causing a surge of sea otter strandings this week in Monterey Bay” and that their staff “safely rescued several pups” after receiving calls from local community members.

Areas of the state still recovering from recent wildfires continue to be at risk for flash flooding, with specific warnings issued for “burn scar” areas including in Big Sur and the Napa valley.

In Los Angeles, city officials warned residents of areas burned by the 2025 Palisades, Sunset and Hurst fires, north of the city, to be prepared for potential evacuation orders starting on Wednesday night, as heavy rains brought increased risk of flooding, mudslide and debris flow.

Statewide, the heaviest of the rainfall was expected north-east of San Francisco, from Santa Rosa to Chico and Redding in the state’s Central valley, and in the southern part of the Bay Area, along coastal mountain ranges from Santa Cruz to San Jose and Palo Alto, according to the National Weather Service.

“Travel delays, localized flooding and hazardous conditions are possible, especially along the coast and on mountain pass roads,” AccuWeather warned in an online forecast.

Atmospheric rivers, massive currents of water vapor that can carry as much or even more water than an actual river, have been growing stronger and deadlier in recent years. In the relatively dry western US, atmospheric river storms provide both essential precipitation and flood risk.

In southern California, the NWS predicted 1-3in of rain in many areas, with 3in-5in in some mountain and foothill areas, and a 20% chance of thunderstorms on Wednesday and Thursday. As much as a foot of snow was expected in higher-elevation areas above 6,000ft. There was a high risk of “significant road flooding” and a moderate risk for rockslides and mudslides, the NWS said.

The risk of coastal wave damage was expected to peak in southern California on Thursday, with additional risks expected next week, with seasonal high tides overlapping with storm risks during Thanksgiving week.

Waterspouts were spotted over the San Francisco Bay earlier this week, and the NWS flagged the risk of additional waterspouts over the ocean east of San Francisco on Wednesday.

title: Obama-era homeless policy fueled crisis it promised to end, expert says as Trump admin makes striking reversal
excerpt:
In an interview with Fox News Digital, homeless services veteran Michele Steeb says rising homelessness despite increased spending exposes deep flaws in the Housing First approach.

The Trump administ...
body_text:
In an interview with Fox News Digital, homeless services veteran Michele Steeb says rising homelessness despite increased spending exposes deep flaws in the Housing First approach.

The Trump administration’s decision to permanently cut federal funding to Los Angeles’ scandal-plagued homeless agency marks a stunning reversal of an Obama-era policy that one expert said produced massive failures.

In an interview with Fox News Digital, homeless services veteran Michele Steeb broke down Tuesday’s announcement from the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) that it is severing ties with the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority (LAHSA).

Steeb said the Housing First model adopted by LAHSA, which provides housing unconditionally without requiring individuals to pursue sobriety or mental health treatment, was championed by former President Barack Obama.

HUD’S HOMELESSNESS REFORMS PUT HUMAN LIVES AHEAD OF HOUSING BUREAUCRACYShe argued the model discouraged recovery by allowing people to remain in subsidized housing indefinitely, leaving fewer available units for others seeking permanent housing.

"So, back in 2013, when they instituted this, President Obama promised that this very different approach would end homelessness in a decade. And a decade later, we were at an almost 35% increase with no accountability," Steeb said, referring to the national homeless population.

Former President Barack Obama championed Housing First, an approach Michele Steeb argues failed to deliver on its promise to end homelessness. (Getty Images/File)

The program ultimately "eliminates purpose from individuals," Steeb said. "They're given housing for life without any requirements."

Earlier this year, Obama called Los Angeles' homelessness crisis a moral "atrocity," arguing that homelessness programs must pair assistance with accountability.

"We should recognize that the average person doesn’t want to have to navigate around a tent city in the middle of downtown," Obama said. "That’s a losing political strategy."

EXCLUSIVE: INSIDE LA'S HOMELESS HELLSCAPE — UNLIKELY CRITICS BLAST DEMS AS GOP HOPEFUL TOURS SKID ROW

California, which adopted the model statewide, offers a particularly striking example of what Steeb views as its shortcomings. Despite significant government investment, homelessness has continued to climb rather than move toward the promised goal of ending it.

Steeb said homelessness in California surged 40% between 2016 and 2025, even as federal spending on homelessness increased at least 200% under the Housing First approach instituted in 2013.

The situation has been particularly stark in Los Angeles, where homelessness climbed between 60% and 70% over the past five years despite LAHSA receiving more than $1 billion in federal funding.

Homelessness climbed despite billions in spending, fueling calls from expert Michele Steeb for greater accountability and treatment requirements. (Allen J. Schaben/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images/File)

LA HOMELESSNESS FRAUD CASES EXPOSE DEEPER PROBLEM THAN STOLEN MILLIONS, OVERSIGHT HAWK WARNS

Steeb said, despite the mounting evidence of failure, defenders of the system continued to blame the homelessness crisis on insufficient funding.

"It's a shame to me that the system, what I often call the homeless industrial complex, is trying to defend it," she said.

"It just has failed so massively. So, there's no excuses except that it was the wrong approach."

Los Angeles County will take over the embattled homeless agency’s responsibilities, though Michele Steeb questions how much the transition will improve services. (Frederic J. Brown/AFP via Getty Images/File)

Steeb said HUD's settlement represents an effort by the Trump administration to restore accountability to homeless services after LAHSA became embroiled in allegations of fraud and financial mismanagement.

The agency's funding will soon be transferred to Los Angeles County, according to officials.

Although Steeb acknowledged the county has its own problems, she hopes the transition could improve a system she believes has failed to address the crisis.

"I'm hopeful. … I think it's better than LAHSA, but I don't think it's going to be that much better," Steeb said.

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

Homelessness climbed despite billions in spending, fueling calls from expert Michele Steeb for greater accountability and treatment requirements. (Allen J. Schaben/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images/File)

LA HOMELESSNESS FRAUD CASES EXPOSE DEEPER PROBLEM THAN STOLEN MILLIONS, OVERSIGHT HAWK WARNS

Steeb said, despite the mounting evidence of failure, defenders of the system continued to blame the homelessness crisis on insufficient funding.

"It's a shame to me that the system, what I often call the homeless industrial complex, is trying to defend it," she said.

"It just has failed so massively. So, there's no excuses except that it was the wrong approach."

Los Angeles County will take over the embattled homeless agency’s responsibilities, though Michele Steeb questions how much the transition will improve services. (Frederic J. Brown/AFP via Getty Images/File)

Steeb said HUD's settlement represents an effort by the Trump administration to restore accountability to homeless services after LAHSA became embroiled in allegations of fraud and financial mismanagement.

The agency's funding will soon be transferred to Los Angeles County, according to officials.

Although Steeb acknowledged the county has its own problems, she hopes the transition could improve a system she believes has failed to address the crisis.

"I'm hopeful. … I think it's better than LAHSA, but I don't think it's going to be that much better," Steeb said.

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Beau Lamarre-Condon’s testimony about Jesse Baird and Luke Davies’ deaths ‘fanciful in the extreme’, crown alleges
excerpt:
Prosecutor argues accused could be convicted on strength of forensic and ballistics evidence alone in closing statement

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condo...
body_text:
Prosecutor argues accused could be convicted on strength of forensic and ballistics evidence alone in closing statement

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon’s claims about the deaths of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies are “fanciful in the extreme”, a court has heard.

The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Baird and his new partner, Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.

He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.

The crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC began delivering his closing statement on Thursday as the double murder trial entered its ninth week.

The defence had argued the two men died in struggles with the accused when he acted in “self-defence”.

Lamarre-Condon had previously told the court he was aiming to shoot Baird in the shoulder to get him to drop a knife, and accidentally shot him a second time as they fell to the ground.

But Hatfield told the court the injury from the first shot would cause someone to pass out.

“Common sense renders it completely improbable that you could suffer such an injury yet immediately grab hold of a pistol with your left and forcefully pull a person brandishing it to the ground,” Hatfield said.

“Such a scenario, you might think, is fanciful in the extreme.”

He argued Lamarre-Condon could be convicted on the strength of the forensic and ballistics evidence alone.

Forensic evidence of the directionality of the bullet and the wounds on Baird’s body indicated Lamarre-Condon shot Baird in the back as the other man fled towards the back door, Hatfield alleged.

The height of the bullet marks meant Baird must have been ducking or stooping at the time, according to the prosecution.

Hatfield said the near-vertical trajectory of the bullet through the floor spoke to a controlled shot through Baird’s temple, with the prosecutor calling it an “execution-style shot”.

The timing between the two shots allowed only for a quick two to three steps, the crown prosecutor told the court.

“Not the bizarre wrestling and yanking the accused has described,” Hatfield said.

At this point, Davies must have realised something was “seriously amiss”, the prosecutor said, and attempted to call triple zero.

There was no doubt he was then killed by a bullet that passed through the door and into his head, Hatfield said, telling the court there was gunshot stippling on the door but not the body.

Aspects of the defence’s case, that Baird lunged at Lamarre-Condon with a knife and that Davies picked up the gun and pointed it at the accused, came only from the former officer himself, Hatfield said.

“Nothing independent of him supports any of what he said about those events,” Hatfield told the jury.

The trial before Justice Natalie Adams continues.

title: No 1 Florida loses to Houston as four of the preseason AP top five fall before Thanksgiving
excerpt:
"This was the worst offseason in the history of college basketball. Because of the chaos. There's no question about it. "

Houston had waited since April 2025 for another shot at Florida. On Wednesday...
body_text:
"This was the worst offseason in the history of college basketball. Because of the chaos. There's no question about it. "

Houston had waited since April 2025 for another shot at Florida. On Wednesday, the Cougars made sure this one would not be decided in the final minute.

No. 8 Houston beat No. 1 Florida 86-76 in Las Vegas, advancing to the Players Era 8 championship game and handing the Gators their first loss of the season. Florida had beaten Houston 65-63 in the 2025 national championship game. Florida’s loss also means four of the preseason AP top five have already been beaten, with Duke losing twice.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Houston Cougars players celebrate against the Florida Gators during the 2026 Players Era Men's Championship at Michelob ULTRA Arena. (Getty Images)

Florida, which was the AP preseason No. 1 and entered the game 5-0, led 40-37 at halftime. Houston took the lead early in the second half before Florida briefly regained the lead at 47-46. But Houston scored the next 11 points and never trailed again, building a lead as large as 14 points.

Dedan Thomas Jr. scored 30 for the Cougars, while Joseph Tugler recorded a 12-point, 10-rebound double-double.

KENTUCKY NEEDS BUZZER-BEATING THREE TO SURVIVE NORTHERN ARIZONA'S UPSET BID AT RUPP ARENA

Kelvin Sampson’s Houston program entered the game ranked eighth and has been among the sport’s contenders for years. Still, beating the team that denied Houston a national title, and doing it while that team sat at No. 1, gives the Cougars a massive November resume boost.

It also makes the analytics look pretty smart. The AP voters had Houston 10th in the preseason, but KenPom rated the Cougars third. After beating Florida by 10 on a neutral floor, Houston looks a lot closer to No. 3 than No. 10.

Florida joins Duke, Illinois and Arizona as preseason AP top five teams that have already lost less than three weeks into the college basketball season. UConn is the lone unbeaten member of that group, at least heading into its Wednesday night visit to Arizona.

Thomas Haugh, who played on Florida’s 2025 national championship team, scored 18 points in Wednesday’s loss to Houston. (Getty Images)

Arizona was the first to fall, losing 84-75 to UCLA on opening night. The Wildcats are ranked No. 12 in this week's poll. A week later, Michigan State beat then-No. 2 Duke 79-73, while Texas Tech knocked off then-No. 3 Illinois 84-78.

Illinois responded Tuesday by going into Duke and winning by 21. The Blue Devils, the preseason No. 2, have now lost twice before Thanksgiving. The Michigan State loss only dropped Duke from No. 2 to No. 5, but expect another fall for the Blue Devils when the Week 4 rankings come out on Nov. 23.

Michigan State’s stay at No. 2 may be short, too. After beating Duke, the Spartans managed just 46 points in a 61-46 loss at No. 14 Tennessee on Tuesday.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

And the trouble has reached beyond the preseason favorites. Unranked Memphis opened its season by beating No. 18 Iowa State 80-76. The Tigers followed that by erasing an 18-point deficit against No. 10 Louisville on Sunday and winning 98-78 after outscoring Louisville by 31 points in the second half.

Joseph Tugler and the No. 8 Houston Cougars upset the No. 1 Florida Gators on Wednesday. (Getty Images)

Over the weekend, LSU went to Gonzaga and beat the then-No. 14 Bulldogs 81-80 on a late shot. On Tuesday, Indiana added an 81-76 win over No. 20 Arkansas.

Kentucky can be grateful it is missing from that list. The Wildcats, who entered the game as 30-point favorites, needed a late three-pointer to escape Northern Arizona 78-77 at Rupp Arena last week, a close call that fit the season’s mood even if it didn't count as another upset.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

None of this settles who will matter in March because there is still a lot of basketball to play. I'm certainly not ready to write off Florida, Duke, Arizona or Illinois because of an early-season hiccup (or two, in Duke's case).

Still, that’s five losses for the preseason AP top five. The voters put Florida first and Michigan State second on Monday. By Wednesday night, both had lost by double digits. Good luck with next Monday’s ballot (If the AP has a spare one, I’ll take it).

title: Tyler Herro's three-words sums up status with ex-teammate Bam Adebayo for first game since punching incident

Colin Cowherd discusses Bam Adebayo’s 83-point explosion against the Washington Wizards, and asks how this game will be remembered.

body_text:
Colin Cowherd discusses Bam Adebayo’s 83-point explosion against the Washington Wizards, and asks how this game will be remembered.

The Miami Heat welcomed the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday night in a matchup that might otherwise blend into the early-season NBA schedule.

But a summer feud involving a former Heat player and one of Miami’s current stars has added an unexpected layer of intrigue to the matchup. In July, tensions between Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro reportedly boiled over in Las Vegas.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Since the dispute between the two NBA stars, questions have lingered over whether Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro had repaired their relationship or whether tensions remained.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro of the Miami Heat exit the court during a delay in a game against the Chicago Bulls at the United Center in Chicago, Illinois, on Jan. 8, 2026. (Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Wednesday marked the first time the two players faced each other since the incident, and Herro was noncommittal when asked about the state of their relationship.

HEAT VS. BUCKS BEST BETS: GIANNIS GETS HIS FIRST SHOT AT MILWAUKEE

"I'm not sure. I haven't talked to him," Herro told reporters Wednesday.

Adebayo and Herro were involved in a physical altercation at an NBA Summer League practice facility, during which the Heat center allegedly struck the Milwaukee Bucks guard in the head area.

A blockbuster deal over this past offseason sent Giannis Antetokounmpo to Miami and Herro to Milwaukee, ending his time as Adebayo’s Heat teammate.

Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro react during the fourth quarter against the Atlanta Hawks at Kaseya Center on March 27, 2025, in Miami, Florida. (Getty Images)

MIAMI HEAT UNVEIL VICE CITY COURT FOR 'GRAND THEFT AUTO VI'-THEMED CLASH WITH MILWAUKEE BUCKS

Herro reflected on his time sharing a locker room with Adebayo, and praised the three-time All-Star's skillset. "Obviously I spent a lot of time with Bam. I admire his game. He's a great player. Can do everything on the floor, guard 1-5. He's gifted offensively."

Sources told ESPN that Adebayo initially confronted Herro over alleged social media comments criticizing his defense. Screenshots circulated online purportedly showed Herro questioning Adebayo’s defensive prowess in an Instagram direct message with a fan.

Milwaukee Bucks guard Tyler Herro drives against Atlanta Hawks guard RayJ Dennis in the first half at Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee, Wis., on Nov. 15, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

Adebayo agreed to a three-year, $166 million extension with Miami in June 2024. The alleged DM also appeared to question whether his nightly defensive effort justified a salary approaching $60 million.

Miami entered Wednesday night with an 8-6 record, while Milwaukee had won just once this season.

title: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190.4m after row over its Nazi history
excerpt:
Sotheby's staff handle the "Châtaigniers en fleurs" painting by Vincent van Gogh at an auction preview in Hong Kong last month

Auction house Sotheby's has sold a painting by Vincent van Gogh for a re...
body_text:
Sotheby's staff handle the "Châtaigniers en fleurs" painting by Vincent van Gogh at an auction preview in Hong Kong last month

Auction house Sotheby's has sold a painting by Vincent van Gogh for a record $190.4m (£144.8m).

The sale of Châtaigniers en fleurs ("Chestnut Trees in Blossom") shatters the renowned artist's previous auction record of $117.2 million set in 2022.

The historic sale in New York on Wednesday comes after an eleventh-hour agreement was reached to resolve a dispute regarding claims the art piece was previously sold under duress during the rise of the Nazis.

Châtaigniers en fleurs was painted in 1890 in the final two months of Van Gogh's life. It is considered one of the most important works of art from that period to remain in private hands, according to Sotheby's.

Sotheby's auction of $180m Van Gogh challenged over claims it was 'sold under duress'

It was not immediately clear who purchased the painting. The BBC has contacted Sotheby's for comment.

The oil painting, which was estimated to carry a value of $180m (£136m) prior to the sale, was put up for auction as part of a set called the Blaquier-Arrieta Collection.

Sotheby's announced in the hours before the auction that it had resolved a dispute between the Blaquier-Arrieta family and the heirs of the Fischer family - the prior German owners of the work - regarding the sale.

Representatives acting for heirs of the Fischer family had claimed the painting may have been sold under duress during the rise of the Nazis.

A lawyer for the family's heirs reportedly wrote to Sotheby's on their behalf, telling the auction house that the painting was sold in Amsterdam before World War Two because of financial losses the Fischer family's publishing company suffered under the Nazis. The BBC has contacted the lawyer for comment.

"In recognition of the painting's complex Nazi-era history and the suffering endured by the Fischer family during the Holocaust, the two families have reached a mutually satisfactory resolution and the work will be sold pursuant to their agreement," Sotheby's said on Wednesday.

Sotheby's website details the provenance of the oil painting and how it has researched the artwork changing hands since 1890.

It says Samuel Fischer - a famous German publisher - acquired it 1909 before it was passed down in his family after his death in 1934.

The painting was deposited with Paul Cassirer in Amsterdam in 1932 or 1933 before it went to Henriette and Marcel Kapferer in Paris in 1936, Sotheby's said.

The Blaquier family acquired it in 1975 and owned it for more than half a century before the latest sale, the auction house said.

title: Unemployment rate jumps to 4.9% – the highest level in five years
excerpt:
Jobless rate rises from 4.7% to 4.9% for October, latest bureau of statistics figures reveal

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Unemployment has surged to 4.9% in October,...
body_text:
Jobless rate rises from 4.7% to 4.9% for October, latest bureau of statistics figures reveal

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Unemployment has surged to 4.9% in October, from 4.7%, in a shock increase that will add to rising worries the economy has passed a tipping point following this year’s five interest rate increases.

New figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed the number of employed people dropped by 43,500 in the month, confounding forecasts for jobs growth and a steady jobless rate.

After starting the year at 4%, unemployment has now lifted to its highest level in five years to approach pre-Covid levels.

Sunny Nguyen, the head of Australia economics at Moody’s Analytics, said “the Aussie labour market has unmistakenly turned”.

Nguyen said the latest data “all but closes the door” on any chance of a pre-Christmas rate hike.

“For the RBA, this lands on a board already split over whether policy has gone far enough,” he said.

“The bank only lifted its unemployment forecast earlier this month to peak above 5% by the end of 2028; the labour market is within sight of that level two years early.”

The shock figures validate warnings from the three dissenting Reserve Bank of Australia board members, who voted against the Melbourne Cup day rate hike and warned of a “materially sharper downturn” in the economy as households struggled to deal with this year’s substantial lift in borrowing costs.

Full-time employment dropped by 2,900 in October, the ABS data showed, and part-time employment by a steeper 40,600 people.

title: Patrick McEnroe joins Rep Tim Walberg to back Team USA Act capping foreign college athletes at 20% of rosters
excerpt:
International Tennis Hall of Fame President Patrick McEnroe speaks at a U.S. Capitol press conference advocating for the TEAM USA Act.

Outside the U.S. Capitol on Wednesday, International Tennis Hall...
body_text:
International Tennis Hall of Fame President Patrick McEnroe speaks at a U.S. Capitol press conference advocating for the TEAM USA Act.

Outside the U.S. Capitol on Wednesday, International Tennis Hall of Fame President Patrick McEnroe backed the TEAM USA Act, calling for a 20% cap on international recruits to safeguard college spots for American kids.

Speaking with OutKick after a joint press conference with House Education and Workforce Committee Chairman Tim Walberg, McEnroe warned that foreign recruits hold nearly 70 percent of Division I tennis spots while U.S. taxpayers train hundreds of rival Olympians.

According to House Education and Workforce Committee data, the number of international athletes receiving college scholarships has nearly tripled since 2001, surging from roughly 8,945 to about 25,000 today.

PATRICK MCENROE ON U.S. OPEN WEED SMELL, TRANS ATHLETES, FOREIGN RECRUITS RESHAPING COLLEGE TENNIS

Without roster limits, college programs have turned into feeders for overseas pros, and only a strict cap can save spots for young Americans.

Standing at the U.S. Capitol with House Education and Workforce Chairman Tim Walberg, tennis legend Patrick McEnroe rallied support for the TEAM USA Act, urging Congress to cap international college athletes at 20 percent and preserve scholarships for American youth. (Photo Credit: Vitamin D Public Relations)

"Well, I think there is a good chance that we can push this through, which would limit the amount of international athletes in our collegiate system to 20%, which I think is quite fair," McEnroe told OutKick.

During Wednesday's press conference, Chairman Walberg pressed the urgency of his bill, formally titled the Training and Education for American Members in University Sports and Athletics Act (H.R. 10351).

McEnroe, who played college tennis at Stanford University in the 1980s, welcomes international competition, but noted that foreign enrollment on varsity rosters has climbed over the past 15 years, crowding American-born players out of U.S. universities.

"The numbers are stratospheric," McEnroe stated.

"I mean, it is closing in on 70% for Division I tennis players. Both male and female are in the mid-60s at the moment, and it is continuing to rise. And you are seeing it in other sports as well. Men's soccer is well over 50% now, and many rosters are pretty much 100% international athletes.

I’M A COLLEGE ATHLETE. THE SYSTEM THAT GAVE ME MY DREAM IS STARTING TO BREAK

Appearing before the House Subcommittee on Higher Education and Workforce Development, ESPN commentator Patrick McEnroe addressed lawmakers on the shrinking presence of American student-athletes in NCAA programs. (Education and Workforce Committee)

"I do not think that is good for the ecosystem of youth sports."

Coaches have privately told McEnroe they welcome a cap to break the cycle, though few will risk their jobs by speaking out. Across college athletics, whether a football coach earns $15 million or a tennis coach makes $150, 000, athletic departments demand immediate wins, and job survival pushes programs toward older overseas talent.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"When you see your big rival down the block getting the best players they can from Europe, well, you are going to say you have got to stay in the game, so you are going to do the same thing," McEnroe explained.

"So in no way do I blame the coaches nor the athletes who are just looking for the opportunity, whether they come from Serbia, England, or Tennessee. But the kids in our country are losing opportunities. That is just the bottom line."

That recruiting arms race is hollowing out American youth sports.

A homegrown player who easily earned a spot on a top 50 tennis roster a decade ago is now shut out, leaving parents of 12- to 14-year-old prospects questioning the steep costs and years of sacrifice required for elite junior training when scholarships go to imported semi-professionals.

Rebuilding that domestic pipeline, McEnroe argued, starts with giving coaches clear guardrails.

Patrick McEnroe speaks onstage during the annual Legends Ball presented by BNP Paribas and NetJets, benefiting the International Tennis Hall of Fame, at Cipriani 42nd Street in New York City on Sept. 7, 2024. (Getty Images for the International Tennis Hall of Fame)

"I think they would like to have a choice where they can get two players on their team that are international, and the rest we can make up with American kids," he noted.

SENATE MOVES TO REIN IN COLLEGE SPORTS 'WILD WEST' WITH SWEEPING NEW RULES FOR PLAYERS, SCHOOLS

"Last time I checked, the college system in sports was not supposed to be professional. I realize we sort of lost the plot there when it comes to football and basketball, but all the Olympic sports should just be training grounds for young kids and places where you can dream, have a goal, accomplish that goal, and get an education."

At Wednesday's press conference, Walberg spotlighted that paradox using the Paris Olympic Games.

While 65% of Team USA athletes had ties to NCAA athletics, only 385 of the 1,036 NCAA Olympians in Paris represented the United States, with the remaining 63% competing for foreign nations.

In effect, U.S. universities backed by state and federal tax dollars are funding the training of athletes who later compete against America on the Olympic stage. McEnroe and Walberg argue foreign governments should fund their own Olympic programs rather than relying on American taxpayers.

Under the TEAM USA Act, a uniform 20 percent cap would apply across every collegiate sport, limiting a 10-player college tennis roster to two international spots. Holding every school and coach to one rule would halt the arms race while preserving most roster spots for American athletes.

Passing the bill requires bipartisan support in the House and Senate, where Sen. Jon Husted (R-OH) introduced companion legislation. Alongside Walberg, McEnroe briefed lawmakers on the roster data, warning that many in Washington remain unaware of how dramatically college sports have shifted.

Without congressional action, McEnroe cautions, opportunities for American families will keep shrinking.

At stake is the future of the 99 percent of college athletes who never turn pro, and whether higher education preserves varsity sports as an avenue for education, character, and upward mobility.

"This is the American collegiate system, right? It is not international. It is not a professional sport," McEnroe told OutKick.

"College sports was started, and has given so many people the opportunity, because of what it is supposed to do, which is help people get an education, better their lives, and be useful members of society. That is why I am here, and that is what I am trying to help and protect."

Patrick McEnroe poses for a photo during the Red Carpet Pre-Show of the International Tennis Hall of Fame 2026 Induction Ceremony on Aug. 29, 2026, in Newport, R.I. (Getty Images)

Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

Alejandro Avila is a longtime writer at OutKick, living in Southern California.

title: German FA backs France’s Diallo for FIFA presidency
excerpt:
The German Football Association (DFB) has said it fully backs French football chief Philippe Diallo’s bid to take over as FIFA president, cementing his support in Europe.

DFB President Bernd Neuendor...
body_text:
The German Football Association (DFB) has said it fully backs French football chief Philippe Diallo’s bid to take over as FIFA president, cementing his support in Europe.

DFB President Bernd Neuendorf announced the endorsement on Wednesday, two days after Diallo, president of the French Football Federation (FFF), accepted UEFA’s support to run against incumbent Gianni Infantino in March. European football’s governing body is eager for change at the top of FIFA.

“Philippe Diallo stands for a responsible approach to football and is determined to tackle the challenges facing the game in the years ahead,” Neuendorf said.

“He has a wealth of experience in international football and is widely respected throughout the European game. His approach to the role and the values he stands for are markedly different from those of the current FIFA president.”

The Dutch football association has also backed Diallo, with many European governing bodies expected to follow suit.

Diallo said on Tuesday that he has the support of countries beyond Europe.

“To beat him [Infantino] you need 106 votes, which is a majority,” he said.

“It is now up to me and my team to go and convince those on other continents, but already since yesterday [Monday] I have received spontaneous signs of strong support which will be revealed in the coming days.”

Infantino, who has led world football’s governing body since 2016 and is seeking a fourth term, has faced widespread opposition since his July attempt to sell stakes in future World Cups to private investors.

Infantino quickly abandoned the proposal in the face of the uproar, but UEFA has since gone to a court in Florida in an attempt to gather evidence for a potential complaint of “criminal mismanagement” against the FIFA president in Switzerland.

Diallo announced in September that the FFF was withdrawing its backing for Infantino in the election, following similar announcements from other European associations. At the time, he said that “the trust placed in the FIFA president has been betrayed”.

Despite repeated calls for his resignation, Infantino maintains he has overwhelming support from member associations worldwide.

“We want football to change for the better. We want a FIFA that serves the game and acts in the interests of all its member associations,” Neuendorf said.

In addition to Diallo, who has headed the FFF since January 2023, Infantino faces challenges from top Japanese football official Kozo Tashima and Ramon Vega, an ex-Switzerland player.

title: Kenya’s milk shortage deepens as drought hits farmers and pushes up prices
excerpt:
Nairobi, Kenya – Milk is becoming harder to find in parts of Kenya as prolonged dry conditions take a toll on dairy farmers, disrupting supplies to major towns and pushing up prices.

In Nairobi, some...
body_text:
Nairobi, Kenya – Milk is becoming harder to find in parts of Kenya as prolonged dry conditions take a toll on dairy farmers, disrupting supplies to major towns and pushing up prices.

In Nairobi, some popular brands have become increasingly difficult to find in shops. A 500ml (1-pint) packet of Tuzo, Dairy Best or Mt Kenya milk sells for 79 to 89 Kenyan shillings ($0.61 to $0.68), but supplies have been limited. New brands have appeared on supermarket shelves at about 65 shillings ($0.50) while some neighbourhood shops visited by Al Jazeera were charging as much as 100 shillings ($0.77) for the same quantity.

The shortage is being felt across the dairy supply chain, from farmers struggling to feed their animals to businesses that depend on a steady supply of fresh milk.

In Kajiado County, southwest of Nairobi, dairy farmers said a prolonged dry spell has sharply reduced milk production over the past three months.

Jennifer Leshinka, a farmer in Bisil, told Al Jazeera that her daily milk production had fallen from 120 litres (32 gallons) to 50 litres (13 gallons). With natural pasture dwindling, she has had to buy hay to feed her animals. Some of her dairy animals have also been moved to neighbouring counties in search of grazing land.

“I supplement the little natural grass with several bales of hay to feed my animals, which has become expensive. A bale of hay is currently retailing between 100 and 150 shillings [$0.77 to $1.15], yet it cannot sustain a mature animal for a day,” Leshinka said.

The pressure is not limited to Kajiado. Diminishing pasture and water supplies are affecting pastoralists in arid and semiarid areas as well as dairy farmers in the highlands, another important milk-producing region.

Jackson Sinkeet, a farmer who supplies raw milk to hotels across the Nairobi metropolitan area, said falling yields have made it difficult to meet orders, even from customers willing to pay higher prices.

He warned that the situation could worsen if dry conditions persist.

The decline in production is also affecting dairy cooperatives, which collect milk from farmers and supply major processors.

Jeremiah Ole Ncharo, Kajiado County’s executive committee member in charge of cooperatives, told Al Jazeera that at least five major women-led dairy cooperatives have reported a 50 percent drop in milk deliveries from their members during the dry period.

He said the reduced volumes were affecting supplies to large milk processors, adding to pressure on the formal market.

In Nairobi, hotelier Joram Kamau said businesses were spending hours queuing at major processors’ depots to obtain rationed milk.

The shortage has also raised concerns about the products available in the market. Kamau said he was worried about the growing presence of powdered milk products whose quality and authenticity he questioned. He said he would rather wait for genuine milk, even if it cost more, than risk buying questionable products and losing customers.

Agriculture Cabinet Secretary Mutahi Kagwe told Al Jazeera that the current shortage was largely linked to prolonged dry conditions, which have reduced the availability of pasture, fodder and water, affecting animal productivity and the amount of milk delivered to processors.

He said Kenya’s dairy industry has continued to grow with national milk production rising from 4.64 billion kilogrammes (10.23 billion pounds) in 2021 to 5.52 billion kilogrammes (12.17 billion pounds) in 2025. Formal milk deliveries also increased from about 802 million litres (212 million gallons) to 1.01 billion litres (267 million gallons) over the same period.

However, more recent figures point to a decline in milk reaching formal processors. Kagwe said monthly deliveries averaged about 83.45 million litres (22 million gallons) in 2025, compared with 74.09 million litres (19.57 million gallons) in September.

He said the decline has affected volumes available for processing, particularly UHT milk, which has a longer shelf life and helps maintain supplies.

However, government market surveillance for the week ending October 30 indicated a slight improvement in UHT milk availability across most parts of the country. Other dairy products, including fermented milk, butter and cheese, were generally available at normal stock levels.

Kagwe said the government was monitoring production, processor stocks, producer prices and retail prices. It was also facilitating regional transfers of milk and dairy products, particularly within the East African Community, while encouraging processors to collect more milk from farmers and cooperatives.

He added that farmers were receiving better prices amid tighter supplies. The average gross producer price rose to about 53.88 shillings ($0.41) per litre (1 quart) in July, compared with an average of 49.58 shillings ($0.38) in 2025.

To address longer-term challenges in the dairy sector, the government is looking at ways to increase production and improve farmers’ resilience.

Kagwe said planned measures included expanding fodder production and conservation, continuing a subsidised artificial insemination programme to improve dairy genetics and distributing milk coolers to organised farmer groups. The restructuring of the state-owned dairy processor New KCC is also expected to improve services to producers and consumers.

The government is also exploring President William Ruto’s proposal to introduce Indian water buffaloes to Kenya as an additional source of milk.

Kagwe told Al Jazeera that the initiative was still at an early stage. Kenya would first need to establish veterinary and import requirements, identify suitable breeds and sources, and bring in a limited number of animals to assess their adaptability and productivity under local conditions.

India, the world’s largest milk producer, relies on buffaloes for about 43 percent of its milk production. Buffalo milk has a relatively high fat and solids content, making it suitable for products such as cheese and butter.

But Kagwe said the proposal should be seen as a medium- to long-term opportunity rather than a response to the current shortage.

For farmers such as Leshinka and Sinkeet, the immediate challenge remains the rising cost of keeping their animals fed and productive. In Nairobi, businesses are still struggling to secure enough milk to meet customer demand.

“The animals’ milk yield has dropped significantly. I am unable to supply my customers, who are willing to pay higher prices, because the milk is simply not available,” Sinkeet told Al Jazeera.

title: India's religious make-up - what a new Pew study says about Hindus and Muslims
excerpt:
An Indian woman lights lamps on the occasion of Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights

India will remain overwhelmingly Hindu for decades to come, but its religious composition is projected to shift gr...
body_text:
An Indian woman lights lamps on the occasion of Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights

India will remain overwhelmingly Hindu for decades to come, but its religious composition is projected to shift gradually.

A new study by the Pew Research Center, projecting the world's religious populations to 2070, estimates that Hindus will make up 76% of India's population by then, down from 79% in 2020, while the Muslim share will rise from 15% to 20%.

The shift is rooted largely in differences in age and fertility: Indian Muslims are younger than Hindus and, on average, have more children.

The Pew projections place India at the centre of a wider demographic shift across South Asia.

Pakistan is expected to overtake Indonesia as the country with the world's largest Muslim-majority population, with India moving into second place. Bangladesh, too, is projected to see substantial growth in its Muslim population.

The study projects the religious composition of the world over the next 50-year period, drawing on data from 201 countries and territories, covering virtually the entire global population.

Muslims offer prayer at the historic Jama Masjid in Delhi

It tracks seven religious groups between 2020 and 2070, assuming recent demographic trends continue. Using census and survey data, it establishes each group's size and age profile in 2020, and factors in differences in fertility and religious switching.

The findings place India at the heart of a changing global religious landscape. The country is expected to have the world's second-largest Muslim population by 2070, after Pakistan, with about 334 million Muslims. Pakistan itself will overtake Indonesia as the country with the largest Muslim population, with an estimated 461 million.

Yet the projections offer little support for the more dramatic narratives sometimes attached to India's changing religious composition.

If current demographic trends continue, the Hindu population in the country is expected to grow by 176 million between 2020 and 2070, the report says. It will continue to account for more than three-quarters of the country's population.

Despite a sharp fall in India's overall fertility, Muslim women still have more children, on average, than Hindu women. Pew attributes the shift primarily to demographic momentum.

Indian Muslims had a median age of 24 in 2020, compared with 29 for Hindus.

Between 2025 and 2030, Pew estimates Muslim women in India will have an average of 2.3 children, against 1.8 among Hindu women.

"We expect religious change in India to be driven almost entirely by long-standing demographic differences between Hindus and Muslims: Muslims are younger and have higher fertility rates," Stephanie Kramer of the Pew Research Center told the BBC.

Hindu devotees offer prayers on the banks of the Sabarmati river in India's Gujarat

"The fertility gap has narrowed considerably – from more than one child per woman in 1992 to about half a child in recent years and is likely to keep shrinking," she said.

"But Hindu fertility is already below the replacement level, while Muslim fertility is projected to remain above it for another two decades." (A replacement level is one at which new births are sufficient to maintain a stable population.)

The projections are hardly surprising, says KS James, an Indian demographer at Princeton University.

"The fertility gap between Muslims and Hindus is well established and it means Muslim population growth is likely to remain faster for the next few decades. But fertility is declining across all religious communities and the gap is expected to narrow further," he told the BBC.

"Ultimately, they will converge," he says, adding that the projections do not point to anything dramatically different in India's demographic trajectory.

Demographers push back against claims, often amplified by Hindu right-wing groups, that Muslims will eventually outnumber Hindus. There is no evidence of any significant religious conversion driving population change in India, they say, and the projections do not support such "alarmist scenarios".

Muslim children dressed in festive attire in India

The wider South Asian picture is equally revealing, according to the report.

Pakistan's Muslim population is projected to more than double to 461 million by 2070, overtaking Indonesia as the world's largest. India will rank second, with 334 million Muslims, while Bangladesh's Muslim population will rise to 218 million. India and Nepal, meanwhile, will remain the world's only Hindu-majority countries.

There appears to be a global story behind these regional shifts.

By 2035, Muslims are projected to overtake Christians as the world's largest religious group, according to the report. By 2070, their numbers are expected to reach 3.64 billion, up from 2.02 billion in 2020.

Christianity, meanwhile, will have just under three billion followers. Muslims will account for 36% of humanity, compared with 26% today.

But the most dramatic transformation may be taking place thousands of miles west of South Asia, in Africa.

Christianity's centre of gravity is moving steadily away from Europe and the Americas towards sub-Saharan Africa.

The report says that if recent trends continue, more than half of the world's Christians are expected to live there by 2070, compared with 31% in 2020. Pew forecasts that the Democratic Republic of Congo will overtake the United States as the country with the largest Christian population.

With more than 1.4 billion people, India overtook China in 2023 in terms of population, according to the UN

The steepest decline is expected to occur in Europe. If current trends continue, by 2070 Europe will be home to 11% of the world's Christian population, down from 22% in 2020, the report says.

The US is projected to lose its Christian majority by 2065, although Christians will remain the country's largest religious group in 2070.

One reason for this changing religious landscape is the growing number of people identifying with no religion.

In UK and France, the "religiously unaffiliated" are projected to become the majority by 2070. South Korea is expected to follow suit.

Yet their share of the world's population is forecast to fall from 24% to 17%, largely because of a decline in China's population.

China accounts for about two-thirds of the world's religiously unaffiliated population. Its expected population decline will more than offset growth in secular populations elsewhere, the report says.

By 2070, there are other unexpected shifts.

The US is projected to become the world's fifth-largest Hindu population, with immigration driving much of its growth.

And Australia's unaffiliated population will overtake Christians as the country's largest group.

Buddhism, meanwhile, faces a demographic squeeze. Its population is expected to fall by more than half in China, Japan and South Korea, reflecting the ageing and shrinking populations of East Asia. Laos and Mongolia are projected to lose their Buddhist majorities.

There are, of course, caveats. These are demographic projections, not predictions of everything that might happen. Pew assumes that recently observed patterns of fertility, migration and religious switching - or conversions -  will continue.

"There are many events that could affect religious group populations (including wars, natural disasters, epidemics and changes in economic or social circumstances) that are not analysed here," the report admits.

India's baseline also required projecting the 2020 religious composition from the 2011 census, because the subsequent census had been delayed

Still, the broad direction is unmistakable.

South Asia will remain indispensable to the world's religious story, not just because of India's enormous Hindu population but because of the growing weight of its Muslim populations. Africa will increasingly shape Christianity's future, while Europe and parts of East Asia become more secular.

Clearly, by 2070, the world's religious landscape may look markedly different, shaped less by conversion than by the uneven arithmetic of births, deaths and migration.

title: Wife and daughter arrested after DNA IDs man whose severed head was found in trash bag
excerpt: Placer County Sheriff Wayne Woo explains how DNA identified a man whose severed head was found by a dog walker in 2022 and how investigators linked his wife and daughter to the case. Credit: Placer Co...
body_text:
Placer County Sheriff Wayne Woo explains how DNA identified a man whose severed head was found by a dog walker in 2022 and how investigators linked his wife and daughter to the case. Credit: Placer County Sheriff's Office

A California woman and her daughter were arrested more than four years after a woman walking her dog found a man's severed head in a trash bag, authorities said.

The Placer County Sheriff’s Office identified the man as Paul Wesley Fitzmaurice Jr., 73, who had never been reported missing. Authorities said his wife and daughter had told relatives the victim was still alive.

His daughter, 45-year-old Mary Fitzmaurice, and his wife, 75-year-old Georgia "Gwenn" Fitzmaurice, were booked into the South Placer Jail on Tuesday, officials said in a news release.

Mary was booked on suspicion of murder and Gwenn on suspicion of being an accessory.

DNA BREAKTHROUGH LEADS TO ARREST IN GRISLY 33-YEAR-OLD COLD CASE INVESTIGATORS NEVER GAVE UP ON

Georgia "Gwenn" Fitzmaurice, left, was booked on suspicion of being an accessory, and Mary Fitzmaurice was booked on suspicion of murder, the Placer County Sheriff’s Office said. (Placer County Sheriff's Office)

The women "kept up the facade to family and friends that Paul was still alive," Placer County Sheriff Wayne Woo said at a news conference Wednesday. He said they continued receiving Fitzmaurice’s Social Security benefits and California public pension after his death.

Woo said the women told some of Fitzmaurice’s estranged relatives "he was being a recluse, and he would disappear for days at a time."

They claimed he "would come back to the house every week or so and stay for a couple of days," Woo said.

In its news release, the sheriff’s office alleged Mary killed her father and the two women "conspired to dispose of his remains."

A forensic illustration depicts the man investigators later identified through DNA as Paul Wesley Fitzmaurice Jr., 73. (Othram Inc.)

At Wednesday’s news conference, Placer County District Attorney Morgan Gire said prosecutors expected to file a murder charge against Mary Fitzmaurice by the end of the day and were weighing additional charges related to the killing and the collection of Fitzmaurice’s benefits.

Asked whether money was a motive, Woo said, "There’s still a lot of investigative work to be done, and I would be speculating on motive at this point."

NEW CALIFORNIA LAW EXPANDS DNA TOOLS FOR MISSING PERSONS INVESTIGATIONS

The Mosquito Fire was burning in the Foresthill area when a dog walker found a severed head in September 2022, Placer County Sheriff Wayne Woo said. The discovery was made away from the fire. (Josh Edelson/AFP via Getty Images)

The dog walker found the bag on Sept. 28, 2022, in the Todd Valley area of Foresthill while the Mosquito Fire was burning nearby. Woo said the discovery drew little attention at the time.

"The people that didn’t forget about this case is the residents of Foresthill and our cold case detectives," Woo said.

The remains were too decomposed for investigators to identify the man. Forensic experts at California State University, Chico, helped produce an artist’s rendering, but it yielded no match in missing-person cases. A search of the national law enforcement DNA database also came up empty.

In January 2024, detectives sent a DNA sample to Othram Labs, which used forensic genetic genealogy to find possible distant relatives. With the FBI’s help, investigators traced the family tree and obtained a DNA sample from an out-of-state relative that helped confirm Fitzmaurice’s identity.

GIRL KNOWN AS 'CHELSEA JANE DOE' ID'D 26 YEARS AFTER MUTILATED BODY FOUND HUNDREDS OF MILES FROM HOME STATE

Placer County Sheriff Wayne Woo speaks at a Nov. 18, 2026, news conference announcing a break in the 2022 Foresthill cold case. (Placer County Sheriff's Office)

Othram said in a news release that Fitzmaurice’s identification marked the 94th publicly announced case in California in which investigators used its technology to identify someone.

The sheriff’s office said in its release that investigators believe Mary killed her father at the family’s Citrus Heights home, which detectives searched Tuesday with help from the FBI.

When asked at the briefing where Fitzmaurice was killed, Woo said, "With evidence that we gathered and collected yesterday, we’ll hopefully determine that."

Woo said the rest of Fitzmaurice’s remains have yet to be found.

"We did not find any remains at the residence yesterday," he said.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.
